# Descriptive stats of the parameters 

```{r}
# Function to create descriptive table with quantiles
create_descriptive_table <- function(df, param_rename = NULL) {
  
  # 1. Describe stats using psych
  desc <- describe(df)
  
  # 2. Calculate quantiles: Q5, Q25, Q75, Q95
  quantiles <- df %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), list(
      Q5 = ~ quantile(., 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q25 = ~ quantile(., 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q75 = ~ quantile(., 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q95 = ~ quantile(., 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
    ))) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = everything(),
      names_to = c("Parameter", "Quantile"),
      names_pattern = "(.*)_(Q5|Q25|Q75|Q95)$"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Quantile,
      values_from = value,
      values_fn = mean
    )
  
  # 3. Prepare descriptive stats table and join quantiles
  desc_paper <- desc %>%
    select(mean, sd, se, median) %>%
    rename(
      M = mean,
      SD = sd,
      SE = se,
      Median = median
    ) %>%
    mutate(Parameter = rownames(.)) %>%
    left_join(quantiles, by = "Parameter")
  
  # 4. Rename parameters if a rename vector is provided
  if (!is.null(param_rename)) {
    desc_paper <- desc_paper %>%
      mutate(Parameter = recode(Parameter, !!!param_rename))
  }
  
  # 5. Reorder columns: Parameter first, then stats
  desc_paper <- desc_paper %>%
    select(Parameter, M, SD, SE, Median, Q5, Q25, Q75, Q95) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.list), ~ unlist(.)))  # clean list-columns
  
  return(desc_paper)
}

# print(nice_full_table, preview = "docx")

nice_short_table

# Create descriptive plots for all parameters in df short_table_data
# Define parameters and display names
key_params_all <- c("rlwm_alpha", "gng_beta", "gng_eps", "foraging_exit_threshold", "phys_k")

# Full mapping: New Name = Old Column Name
param_rename_full <- c(
  "RLWM α" = "rlwm_alpha",
  "GNG β" = "gng_beta",
  "GNG ε" = "gng_eps",
  "Foraging Exit Threshold" = "foraging_exit_threshold",
  "Effort κ" = "phys_k"
)

# Split into two groups based on scale
group_small <- c("gng_beta","foraging_exit_threshold")      
group_large <- c("phys_k", "rlwm_alpha","gng_eps")     

# Define a fixed color vector matching the order of your renamed parameters
# Order must match the order in param_rename_full (or we'll map by name later)
fixed_colors <- c(
  "RLWM α" = "#AEC7E8",   # Pastel Blue
  "GNG β" = "#FFBB78",    # Pastel Orange
  "GNG ε" = "#98DF8A",    # Pastel Green
  "Foraging Exit Threshold" = "#FF9896", # Pastel Red
  "Effort κ" = "#C5B0D5"  # Pastel Purple/Brownish (or use "#DDBEA9" for true pastel brown)
)

# Function to create a boxplot with jittered points and hard-coded colors
create_boxplot_jitter <- function(data, params, title_suffix) {
  # 1. Select only the columns we want
  data_subset <- data %>% select(all_of(params))
  
  # 2. Create a safe rename vector for ONLY these parameters
  rename_vec <- param_rename_full[param_rename_full %in% params]
  
  # 3. Rename and reshape
  plot_data <- data_subset %>%
    rename(!!!rename_vec) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Parameter", values_to = "Value")
  
  # Convert Parameter to a factor to control order
  plot_data$Parameter <- factor(plot_data$Parameter, levels = unique(plot_data$Parameter))
  
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Parameter, y = Value, fill = Parameter)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.6, color = "black", size = 1.5) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.color = NA, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.6) +
    
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Parameter value",
      title = paste("Distribution of Key Model Parameters:", title_suffix)
    ) +
    # Apply hard-coded colors by name
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = fixed_colors,
      limits = levels(plot_data$Parameter)
    )+
    # Force y-axis to start at 0
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) 
}

# Create and print both plots
p_small <- create_boxplot_jitter(data_day1, group_small, "")
p_large <- create_boxplot_jitter(data_day1, group_large, "")

# Display plots
print(p_small)
print(p_large)
# Optional: Save to file
# ggsave("parameter_boxplot.png", p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)

```

# Parameter correlations

```{r}
data_day1_cor <- correlation(data_day1, method = "spearman", p_adjust = "none")

data_day1_cor_plot <- data_day1_cor %>%
  summary(redundant = TRUE) %>%
  plot() +
    theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(data_day1_cor_plot)

param_names <- colnames(data_day1[-1])

rlwm_params <- grep("^rlwm_", param_names, value = TRUE)
gng_params  <- grep("^gng_",  param_names, value = TRUE)
phys_params <- grep("^phys_", param_names, value = TRUE)

rlwm_pairs <- combn(rlwm_params, 2, simplify = FALSE)
gng_pairs  <- combn(gng_params,  2, simplify = FALSE)
phys_pairs <- combn(phys_params, 2, simplify = FALSE)

task_pairs <- c(rlwm_pairs, gng_pairs, phys_pairs)

for (p in task_pairs) {
 a <-  plot(cor_test(data_day1, p[1], p[2], method = "spearman"))
 print(a)
}
```

# Day 1

### EFA


```{r day1}
data_day1_constrained_quadratic_full_quests <- data_day1_quests
data_day1_constrained_quadratic_full <- data_day1
 data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_full

 data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_full_quests 


# Factor analysis using factanal
fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, foraging_exit_threshold, phys_k)  # Exclude non-FA relevant columns




# EFA subject vector
EFA_subjID <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg$subjID



# DO PCA and screeplot
pca_result <- prcomp(fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Base R scree plot
screeplot(pca_result, type = "lines", main = "Scree Plot")

# Do a paralell analysis to determine the number of factors
fa_parallel <- fa.parallel(fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg, fa = "fa", n.iter = 100)

fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg <- factanal(
  fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg,
  factors = 2,
  rotation = "varimax",
  scores = "regression"
)

fa(
  fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg,
  nfactors = 2,
  rotate = "varimax",
  fm="pa"
)



print(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg)
print(loadings(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg), cutoff = 0)


# Factor analysis using principal factor solution
fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_pa <- fa(fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg,nfactors=2,fm="pa",rotate = "varimax")

## Print nice factor analysis ##
fa_temp <- fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_pa$loadings[, 1:2] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(Parameter = rownames(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_pa$loadings)) %>%
  mutate(Parameter = recode(Parameter,
                           "rlwm_alpha" = "RLWM Alpha",
                           "gng_beta" = "GNG Beta",
                           "gng_eps" = "GNG Epsilon",
                           "foraging_exit_threshold" = "Foraging Exit Threshold",
                           "phys_k" = "Effort Kappa")) %>%
  mutate("Factor 1" = PA1, "Factor 2" = PA2)%>%
  select(-PA1, -PA2)

nice_table(fa_temp)

#### Testing 1 factor solution of vigor params ####
```

```{r day1_cor_1}
  filter(Parameter1 %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa") & !Parameter2 %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa"))

# Print a matrix
correlation_matrix_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_reduced %>%
  summary(redundant = FALSE) %>%
  plot() 

# Flip if needed so all variables are in a consistent column
corr_clean <- corr_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    variable = if_else(Parameter1 %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa"), Parameter2, Parameter1),
    factor   = if_else(Parameter1 %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa"), Parameter1, Parameter2)
  ) %>%
  select(factor, variable, rho, CI_low, CI_high, p)


corr_clean <- corr_clean %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p < 0.05  ~ "*",
    TRUE      ~ ""
  ))

corr_clean$variable <- factor(corr_clean$variable, levels = c(
  "behavioral_activation",
  "emotional_sensitivity",
  "social_motivation",
  "Score_ASRM",
  "Score_CESD",
  "Score_SHPS"
))

  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", rho), sig)), size = 7) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "pink", mid = "white", high = "light blue",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Spearman's ρ"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Vigor and RL with Questionnaires",
    x = "Latent Factor",
    y = "Variable"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  coord_fixed()

  filter(!variable %in% c("social_motivation", "emotional_sensitivity"))

  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", rho), sig)), size = 7) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "pink", mid = "white", high = "light blue",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Spearman's ρ"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Vigor and RL with Questionnaires",
    x = "Questionnaire",
    y = "Latent Factor"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) 

# Step 1: Filter only the 8 correlations of interest
holm_df_OG <- corr_clean %>%
  filter(variable %in% c("Score_CESD", "Score_ASRM", "Score_SHPS", "behavioral_activation")) %>%
  filter(factor %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa")) %>%
  arrange(p)  # Optional: sort for clearer view

# Step 1: Filter only the 8 correlations of interest
holm_df <- corr_clean %>%
  filter(variable %in% c("Score_CESD", "Score_ASRM", "behavioral_activation")) %>%
  filter(factor %in% c("factor1_pa", "factor2_pa")) %>%
  arrange(p)  # Optional: sort for clearer view


# Step 2: Apply Holm correction
holm_df <- holm_df %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"))

# Step 3: Add corrected significance stars
holm_df <- holm_df %>%
  mutate(sig_holm = case_when(
    p_holm < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p_holm < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p_holm < 0.05  ~ "*",
    TRUE           ~ ""
  ))

# View results
print(holm_df)

paper_cor_horizontal <- ggplot(holm_df, aes(x = variable, y = factor, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", rho), sig_holm)), size = 7) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "pink", mid = "white", high = "light blue",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Spearman's ρ"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Vigor and RL with Questionnaires",
    x = "Questionnaire",
    y = "Latent Factor"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
# Extract loadings matrix
loadings <- as.data.frame(unclass(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_pa$loadings))

# Add variable names as a column
loadings$Variable <- rownames(loadings)

# Reshape to long format for ggplot
loadings_long <- pivot_longer(loadings, 
                              cols = starts_with("PA"), 
                              names_to = "Factor", 
                              values_to = "Loading")

loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable, !!!param_rename))

# Optional: reorder variables by absolute loading for better visualization
loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = rev(unique(Variable))))

loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Factor = recode(Factor, "PA1" = "RL", "PA2" = "Vigor"))


# --- 1. DATA PREPARATION ---
loadings <- as.data.frame(unclass(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_pa$loadings))
loadings$Variable <- rownames(loadings)

loadings_long <- pivot_longer(loadings, 
                              cols = starts_with("PA"), 
                              names_to = "Factor", 
                              values_to = "Loading")

# Rename Factors
loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Factor = recode(Factor, "PA1" = "RL", "PA2" = "Vigor"))

# --- 2. FORCE NEW NAMES BY ORDER ---
unique_vars <- unique(loadings_long$Variable)
desired_names <- c(
  "RLWM α", 
  "GNG β", 
  "GNG ε", 
  "Effort κ", 
  "Foraging Exit Threshold"
)

force_map <- setNames(desired_names, unique_vars[1:5])

loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable, !!!force_map))

# --- 3. FORCE SPECIFIC ORDER (CORRECTED FOR FLIP) ---
# With coord_flip(), the FIRST item in 'levels' is at the BOTTOM.
# You want visual order (Top to Bottom): RLWM, GNG β, GNG ε, Foraging, Effort κ.
# So 'levels' must be (Bottom to Top): Effort κ, Foraging, GNG ε, GNG β, RLWM.
ordered_levels <- c(
  "Effort κ", 
  "Foraging Exit Threshold", 
  "GNG ε", 
  "GNG β", 
  "RLWM α"
)

loadings_long <- loadings_long %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = ordered_levels))

# --- 4. FACET LABELS ---
facet_labels <- c(
  "RL" = "RL\n15% explained variance",
  "Vigor" = "Vigor\n5% explained variance"
)

# --- 5. PLOT ---
p <- ggplot(loadings_long, aes(x = Variable, y = Loading, fill = Factor)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "identity", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.3, 0.3), color = "black", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  facet_wrap(~ Factor, nrow = 1, scales = "fixed", labeller = as_labeller(facet_labels)) +
  labs(title = "", x = "Parameters", y = "Factor loadings") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) + 
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "cm"),      # space between facets
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

print(p)
```

### Bayesian SEM

Exploratory analysis to see whether we are able to fit SEM on our data when specifying priors based on our pilot study.

```{r,eval=FALSE}



#### Tighter Priors ####
# 1. Define the Model with Tighter Priors
# Note: SDs are calculated as (CI_Width / 4) / 2
model_final <- '
  # --- Measurement Model ---
  
  # RL Factor
  # gng_beta: CI [8.4, 79.2] -> Width=70.8 -> SD=17.7 (Used 13.0 / 2 )
  # gng_eps:  CI [-23.9, 1.6] -> Width=25.5 -> SD=6.4 (Used 5.0 / 2)
  
  RL =~ rlwm_alpha + 
        prior("normal(19.6, 6.5)")*gng_beta + 
        prior("normal(-4.8, 2.5)")*gng_eps
  
  # Vigor Factor
  # phys_k:   CI [-0.62, 0.04] -> Width=0.66 -> SD=0.165 (Used 0.12 / 2)
  # gng_eps:  CI [0.01, 3.35] -> Width=3.34 -> SD=0.84 (Used 0.6 / 2)
  
  Vigor =~ foraging_exit_threshold + 
           prior("normal(-0.11, 0.6)")*phys_k + 
           prior("normal(0.50, 0.3)")*gng_eps
  


'

# 2. Run the Model
# Arguments: burnin (warmup) + sample (post-warmup)
fit_final <- bcfa(model_final, 
                  data = data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests,
                  n.chains = 4, 
                  burnin = 2000,    # Warmup iterations
                  sample = 8000,    # Sampling iterations (Total = 8000)
                  seed = 12345)     # Optional: for reproducibility

# 3. Check Diagnostics
summary(fit_final, psrf = TRUE, neff = TRUE)


# Plot the measurement model for Day 1
lavaanPlot(fit_final, coefs = TRUE, stand = FALSE, covs = TRUE, stars = c("latent","covs"),graph_options = list(rankdir = "TB"))

# Estimate the goodness of the fit
blavInspect(fit_final, "rhat")
blavInspect(fit_final, "neff")
fitm_fitfinal <- fitmeasures(fit_final)


### Wider priors ###
# 1. Define the Model with wider Priors
# Note: SDs are calculated as (CI_Width / 4)
model_final_wider <- '
  # --- Measurement Model ---
  
  # RL Factor
  # gng_beta: CI [8.4, 79.2] -> Width=70.8 -> SD=17.7 (Used 13.0 for tighter stability)
  # gng_eps:  CI [-23.9, 1.6] -> Width=25.5 -> SD=6.4 (Used 5.0 for tighter stability)
  
  RL =~ rlwm_alpha + 
        prior("normal(19.6, 13)")*gng_beta + 
        prior("normal(-4.8, 5)")*gng_eps
  
  # Vigor Factor
  # phys_k:   CI [-0.62, 0.04] -> Width=0.66 -> SD=0.165 (Used 0.12)
  # gng_eps:  CI [0.01, 3.35] -> Width=3.34 -> SD=0.84 (Used 0.6)
  
  Vigor =~ foraging_exit_threshold + 
           prior("normal(-0.11, 0.12)")*phys_k + 
           prior("normal(0.50, 0.6)")*gng_eps
  


'

# 2. Run the Model
# Arguments: burnin (warmup) + sample (post-warmup)
fit_final_wider <- bcfa(model_final_wider, 
                  data = data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests,
                  n.chains = 4, 
                  burnin = 2000,    # Warmup iterations
                  sample = 8000,    # Sampling iterations (Total = 8000)
                  seed = 12345)     # Optional: for reproducibility

# 3. Check Diagnostics
summary(fit_final_wider, psrf = TRUE, neff = TRUE)


# Plot the measurement model for Day 1
lavaanPlot(fit_final_wider, coefs = TRUE, stand = FALSE, covs = TRUE, stars = c("latent","covs"),graph_options = list(rankdir = "TB"))

blavInspect(fit_final_wider, "rhat")
blavInspect(fit_final_wider, "neff")
fitm_fitfinal <- fitmeasures(fit_final_wider)

### No priors ###
# 1. Define the Model with no Priors
model_final_nopriors <- '
  # --- Measurement Model ---
  
  # RL Factor

  RL =~ rlwm_alpha + 
        gng_beta + 
        gng_eps
  
  # Vigor Factor
  Vigor =~ foraging_exit_threshold + 
           phys_k + 
           gng_eps
  


'

# 2. Run the Model
# Arguments: burnin (warmup) + sample (post-warmup)
fit_final_nopriors <- bcfa(model_final_nopriors, 
                  data = data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests,
                  n.chains = 4, 
                  burnin = 2000,    # Warmup iterations
                  sample = 8000,    # Sampling iterations (Total = 8000)
                  seed = 12345)     # Optional: for reproducibility

# 3. Check Diagnostics
summary(fit_final_nopriors, psrf = TRUE, neff = TRUE)


# Plot the measurement model for Day 1
lavaanPlot(fit_final_nopriors, coefs = TRUE, stand = FALSE, covs = TRUE, stars = c("latent","covs"),graph_options = list(rankdir = "TB"))

blavInspect(fit_final_nopriors, "rhat")
blavInspect(fit_final_nopriors, "neff")
fitm_fitfinal <- fitmeasures(fit_final_nopriors)

# Compare the models
```

# Validity of EFA

Inspect that the reason that the factor structure in day 2 is not preserved is not just sample size, i.e., do EFA on the same sample on day 1 and day 2 and compare.

```{r}
data_day1_with_only_day2_participants <- 
data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg %>%
  filter(subjID %in% data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg$subjID) %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, foraging_exit_threshold, phys_k)

# Perform 2 factor EFA
data_day1_with_only_day2_participants_fa <- factanal(data_day1_with_only_day2_participants, factors = 2)
print(data_day1_with_only_day2_participants_fa)

data_day1_with_only_day2_participants_fa_pa <- fa(data_day1_with_only_day2_participants, nfactors = 2, fm = "pa")
print(data_day1_with_only_day2_participants_fa_pa$loadings)

## And now let's do the EFA on the remaining participants from day 1 that were not
# in day 2
data_day1_with_no_day2_participants <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg %>%
  filter(!subjID %in% data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg$subjID) %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, foraging_exit_threshold, phys_k)

# Do again 2 factor EFA
data_day1_with_no_day2_participants_fa <- factanal(data_day1_with_no_day2_participants, factors = 2)
print(data_day1_with_no_day2_participants_fa)

data_day1_with_no_day2_participants_fa_pa <- fa(data_day1_with_no_day2_participants, nfactors = 2, fm = "pa")
```

### ICC of EFA

```{r icc-constrained-quadratic-prg}
###### Loadings method ######
# Which factoring method to use ml/pa
fm_method <- "pa"  # "ml" or "pa"

# Make an intersection of PRG exclusion factor scores both for day 1 and day 2
if (fm_method == "ml") {
  data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors %>%
    select(subjID, factor1, factor2) %>%
    filter(subjID %in% data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors$subjID)
  
  data_icc_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores <- data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors %>%
    select(subjID, factor1, factor2)
  
} else if (fm_method == "pa") {
   data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors %>%
    select(subjID, factor1_pa, factor2_pa) %>%
    filter(subjID %in% data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors$subjID)
  
  data_icc_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores <- data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_with_factors %>%
    select(subjID, factor1_pa, factor2_pa)
}


# Make an intersection of PRG exclusion data of day 1 that are also in day 2
data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_retest <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg %>%
  filter(subjID %in% data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg$subjID)

# Make an intersection of PRG exclusion data of day 2 that are also in day 1
data_icc_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_retest <- data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg %>%
  filter(subjID %in% data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg$subjID)

# Get factor scores for participants on day 2 given the loadings from day 1 (if you wanna reproduce older results comment this section and it will use the original factor scores)
fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_new <- fa(fa_data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg, nfactors = 2, fm = fm_method, rotate = "varimax")
fa_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_new <- fa(fa_data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg, nfactors = 2, fm = fm_method, rotate = "varimax")

# Get loadings from the Day 1 FA
fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_loadings <- fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_new$loadings[,1:2]

# Get loadings from the Day 2 FA
fa_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_loadings <- fa_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_new$loadings[,1:2]

# Reduce the data to only the relevant columns
data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_reduced <- data_icc_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_retest %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, foraging_exit_threshold,phys_k)

# Get factor scores for day 2 given the loadings from day 1
fa_scores_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg <- factor.scores(data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_reduced, fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_loadings, method = "Thurstone")
fa_scores_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_scores <- fa_scores_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg$scores

# Calculate ICC for each day and model
factor1 <-  icc(cbind(data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores[,2],fa_scores_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_scores[,1]), model = "twoway", type = "agreement", unit = "single")
factor2 <-  icc(cbind(data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_factor_scores[,3],fa_scores_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_scores[,2]), model = "twoway", type = "agreement", unit = "single")
icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("Factor1", "Factor2"),
  CI_upper = c(factor1$ubound, factor2$ubound),
  CI_lower = c(factor1$lbound, factor2$lbound),
  ICC = c(factor1$value, factor2$value)
)

icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df

# Make a nice table out of it
# Rename Factor1 to Factor 1 (RL) and Factor 2 (Vigor)
icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$Factor <- recode(icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$Factor, 
                                                   "Factor1" = "Factor 1 (RL)", 
                                                   "Factor2" = "Factor 2 (Vigor)")

nice_icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df <- nice_table(icc_constrained_quadratic_prg_df)

###### Correlation of loadings ######

fac2_cor_constr_quadratic_prg <- cor(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_loadings[,2], fa_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_loadings[,2], method = "spearman")
print(fac1_cor_constr_quadratic_prg)

###### ICC of parameters ######
# Get the common column names between df_1_retest_pp and df_2
variables <- intersect(names(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg), names(data_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg))
variables <- variables[!variables %in% c("subjID")]  # Exclude factor columns

# List to store ICC results
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg <- list()
for (variable in variables) {
  icc_result <- icc(cbind(data_icc_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_retest[[variable]], data_icc_day2_constrained_quadratic_prg_retest[[variable]]), 
                    model = "twoway", type = "agreement", unit = "single")
  
  icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg[[variable]] <- list(Variable = variable, 
                                                            LB = round(icc_result$lbound, 2), 
                                                            UB = round(icc_result$ubound, 2),
                                                            ICC = round(icc_result$value, 2))
}

# Convert list to dataframe
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df <- do.call(rbind, icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg)
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df <- as.data.frame(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Fix the Variable column
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$Variable <- rownames(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df)  # Use row names as the correct variable names
rownames(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df) <- NULL  # Remove row names after extraction
# Convert numeric columns
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$LB <- as.numeric(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$LB)
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$UB <- as.numeric(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$UB)
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$ICC <- as.numeric(icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df$ICC)
icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df

# Make an output in nice_table
nice_icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df <- icc_params_constrained_quadratic_prg_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% c("rlwm_alpha", "gng_beta", "gng_eps", "foraging_exit_threshold", "phys_k")) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = recode(Variable,
      "rlwm_alpha" = "RLWM Alpha",
      "gng_beta" = "GNG Beta",
      "gng_eps" = "GNG Epsilon",
      "foraging_exit_threshold" = "Foraging Exit Threshold",
      "phys_k" = "Effort Kappa"
    ),
    CI_lower = LB,
    CI_upper = UB
  ) %>%
  select(Variable,  ICC,CI_lower, CI_upper)

# Make a nice table out of it
```

### ICC of questionnaires

Let's check how realiable the questionnaires were in order to estimate how "noisy" they are.

```{r}
# Make the "common" participants dfs for day 1 and day 2
quest_icc_day1 <- quest_data_day1_full_id %>%
  filter(subjID %in% quest_data_day2_full_id$subjID)

quest_icc_day2 <- quest_data_day2_full_id %>% # Match it, just checking
  filter(subjID %in% quest_icc_day1$subjID)

# Do ICC 
# Get all variable names except subjID
vars <- setdiff(names(quest_icc_day1), "subjID")

# Run ICC for each variable and store in a dataframe
quest_icc_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
  dat <- data.frame(day1 = quest_icc_day1[[v]], 
                    day2 = quest_icc_day2[[v]])
  res <- icc(dat, model = "twoway", type = "agreement", unit = "single")
  
  data.frame(
    variable = v,
    ICC = res$value,
    CI_lower = res$lbound,
    CI_upper = res$ubound
  )
}))
print(quest_icc_df)
```

#### Z-Score method

```{r}
# Pivot data to long format
var_order <- names(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized)[-1]

df_long <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -subjID,
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "zscore"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    variable = factor(variable, levels = var_order),
    outlier = abs(zscore) > 3
  )

# Identify subjects who are outliers in any variable
outlier_subjects <- df_long %>%
  filter(outlier) %>%
  pull(subjID) %>%
  unique()

# Split data for plotting layers
df_other <- df_long %>% filter(!(subjID %in% outlier_subjects))
df_highlight <- df_long %>% filter(subjID %in% outlier_subjects)

# Assign colors to outlier subjects

  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(length(outlier_subjects), "Set1"),

)

# Build the plot

  # Boxplots behind points
  geom_boxplot(
    data = df_long, 
    aes(x = variable, y = zscore),
    alpha = 0.2,
    outlier.shape = NA  # hide default outlier dots
  ) +
  
  # Cutoff lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-3, 3), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Non-outlier subjects (black, smaller)
  geom_point(data = df_other, aes(x = variable, y = zscore), 
             color = "black", size = 2) +
  
   # Lines connecting outlier subjects
  geom_line(data = df_highlight,

             aes(x = variable, y = zscore, color = subjID),

  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette,
                     name = "Outlier Subject ID") +
  
  # Theme
```

#### IQR Method

```{r}

#### Assess the univariete outliers of the parameters using IQR * 1.5 fences #####
# Melt data to long format
numeric_cols <- sapply(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized, is.numeric)
df_long <- melt(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized, 
                id.vars = "subjID", 
                measure.vars = names(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized)[numeric_cols])

# Compute IQR outliers for each variable
thresholds_df <- df_long %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    Q1 = quantile(value, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

outliers_df <- df_long %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(value, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,
    is_outlier = value < lower | value > upper
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Identify all subjects who are outliers in any variable
iqr_outliers_ids <- unique(outliers_df$subjID[outliers_df$is_outlier])

# Split data: outlier subjects vs others
df_other <- df_long %>% filter(!(subjID %in% iqr_outliers_ids))
df_highlight <- df_long %>% filter(subjID %in% iqr_outliers_ids)

# Assign colors to lines for outlier subjects
color_palette <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(length(iqr_outliers_ids)),
  iqr_outliers_ids
)

# Build the plot
out_iqr_day1 <- ggplot() +
  # Boxplots behind everything
  geom_boxplot(
    data = df_long,
    aes(x = variable, y = value),
    alpha = 0.2,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  
  # Red lines for IQR thresholds
  geom_segment(data = thresholds_df,
               aes(x = as.numeric(factor(variable)) - 0.4, 
                   xend = as.numeric(factor(variable)) + 0.4,
                   y = lower, yend = lower),
               color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(data = thresholds_df,
               aes(x = as.numeric(factor(variable)) - 0.4, 
                   xend = as.numeric(factor(variable)) + 0.4,
                   y = upper, yend = upper),
               color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Non-outlier subjects (black points)
  geom_point(data = df_other, aes(x = variable, y = value),
             color = "black", size = 2) +
  
  # Lines connecting outlier subjects across variables
  geom_line(data = df_highlight,
            aes(x = variable, y = value, group = subjID, color = subjID),
            size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Points for the outlier subjects
  geom_point(data = df_highlight,
             aes(x = variable, y = value, color = subjID),
             size = 3) +
  
  # Color scale for outlier subjects
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette,
                     name = "Outlier Subject ID") +
  
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Value") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

out_iqr_day1

data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_outliers_IQR <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized %>%

# Factor analysis using factanal without the uni outliers
```

### Skewness-adjusted boxplots

Boxplots adjusted for skewed distributions as proposed in Hubert and Vandervieren (2008)

```{r}

adjbox(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1])

# Prepare data
data_values <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1]
subjIDs <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized$subjID

# Compute adjusted boxplot stats for each variable
stats_list <- lapply(data_values, adjboxStats)
names(stats_list) <- colnames(data_values)

# Build a dataframe of boxplot stats + fences for ggplot
boxplot_stats <- lapply(names(stats_list), function(var) {
  s <- stats_list[[var]]
  data_var <- data_values[[var]]
  data.frame(
    variable = var,
    ymin = min(data_var[data_var >= s$fence[1]], na.rm = TRUE),  # lowest non-outlier
    lower = s$stats[2],      # Q1
    middle = s$stats[3],     # median
    upper = s$stats[4],      # Q3
    ymax = max(data_var[data_var <= s$fence[2]], na.rm = TRUE),   # highest non-outlier
    lower_fence = s$fence[1],  # skew-adjusted lower fence
    upper_fence = s$fence[2]   # skew-adjusted upper fence
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Create long dataframe for points and outlier labeling
df_long <- data_values %>%
  mutate(subjID = subjIDs) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -subjID, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    is_outlier = value %in% stats_list[[variable]]$out
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Identify outlier subjects
outlier_subjects <- df_long %>%
  filter(is_outlier) %>%
  pull(subjID) %>%
  unique()

# Assign darker colors to outlier subjects
color_palette <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))(length(outlier_subjects)),
  outlier_subjects
)

# Define variable order
var_order <- c("rlwm_alpha", "gng_beta", "gng_eps", "foraging_exit_threshold", "phys_k")
df_long$variable <- factor(df_long$variable, levels = var_order)
boxplot_stats$variable <- factor(boxplot_stats$variable, levels = var_order)

# Split data for plotting
df_other <- df_long %>% filter(!(subjID %in% outlier_subjects))
df_highlight <- df_long %>% filter(subjID %in% outlier_subjects)

# Plot
ggplot() +
  # Boxplots
  geom_boxplot(
    data = boxplot_stats,
    aes(
      x = variable, 
      ymin = ymin, lower = lower, middle = middle, upper = upper, ymax = ymax
    ),
    stat = "identity", fill = "lightgray", color = "black"
  ) +
  
  # Add skewness-adjusted fences
  geom_segment(
    data = boxplot_stats,
    aes(x = as.numeric(variable) - 0.4, xend = as.numeric(variable) + 0.4,
        y = lower_fence, yend = lower_fence),
    color = "red", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = boxplot_stats,
    aes(x = as.numeric(variable) - 0.4, xend = as.numeric(variable) + 0.4,
        y = upper_fence, yend = upper_fence),
    color = "red", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  # Non-outlier points
  geom_point(
    data = df_other, 
    aes(x = variable, y = value),
    size = 2, color = "black"
  ) +
  
  # Outlier subjects (points + connecting lines)
  geom_line(
    data = df_highlight,
    aes(x = variable, y = value, group = subjID, color = subjID),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = df_highlight,
    aes(x = variable, y = value, color = subjID),
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  # Colors + theme
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, name = "Outlier Subjects") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Z score", limits = c(NA, 5)) +   # <-- added this
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

medcouple_outliers <- df_long %>%
  filter(is_outlier) %>%
  pull(subjID) %>%
  unique()

data_day1_no_medcouple_outliers <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized %>%
  filter(!subjID %in% medcouple_outliers)
 

# Do the factor analysis without the medcouple outliers
fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_medcouple_outliers <- factanal(
  data_day1_no_medcouple_outliers[,-1],
  factors = 2,
  rotation = "varimax",
  scores = "regression"
)
print(loadings(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_medcouple_outliers),cutoff=0)

no_medcouple_out_efa_pa <- fa(data_day1_no_medcouple_outliers[,-1], nfactors=2, fm="pa",rotate="varimax")
no_medcouple_out_efa_pa$loadings
```

```{r}
  # Outlier points (colored)
  geom_point(data = df_highlight,
             aes(x = variable, y = zscore, color = subjID),
             size = 4) +
  
  # Color scale for outlier subjects
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette,
                     name = "Outlier Subject ID") +
  
  # Theme and labels
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Z-score") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

outlier_plot_day1_measures

# Pull the behavioural outliers 
behavioural_outliers_day1 <- df_long_data1_measures %>%
  filter(outlier == TRUE) %>%
  select(subjID) %>%

# 7 in total using the z score method
behavioural_outliers_day1

# How many of those behavioural outliers are also included in the parameters outliers
```

# Multivariete outliers (Day 1)

```{r}
# Assess the multivariete outliers of the params using Mahalanobis distance
# Compute mean vector and covariance matrix
mu <- colMeans(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1], na.rm = TRUE)
cov_mat <- cov(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1], use = "complete.obs")

# Compute Mahalanobis distance for each row
# Source: https://builtin.com/data-science/mahalanobis-distance
md <- mahalanobis(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1], center = mu, cov = cov_mat)
cutoff <- qchisq(0.95, df = ncol(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized[,-1]))  # p < .05 threshold


# Flag potential multivariate outliers
outliers <- which(md > cutoff)


# Add results back to dataframe
df_plot <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized
df_plot$mahal_dist <- md
df_plot$outlier <- md > cutoff

# Boxplot with jittered points
multi_out_plot_day1 <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = "Participant", y = mahal_dist)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "lightgray", color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = outlier), width = 0.15, size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cutoff, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +

  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red")) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Mahalanobis Distance",
    title = ""
  )
print(multi_out_plot_day1)

mahalanobis_out <- df_plot$subjID[df_plot$outlier]

#DO Fa without mahalanobis outliers
data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_mahalanobis_outliers <- data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized %>%
  filter(!subjID %in% mahalanobis_out)

fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_mahalanobis_outliers <- factanal(
  data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_mahalanobis_outliers[,-1],
  factors = 2,
  rotation = "varimax",
  scores = "regression"
)

print(fa_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_mahalanobis_outliers)

no_multivar_out_efa_pa <- fa(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_normalized_no_mahalanobis_outliers[,-1], nfactors = 2, fm="pa",rotate = "varimax")
no_multivar_out_efa_pa$loadings
```

```{r}
# Load the subjective ratings for each task
tasks <- c("foraging","gng","rlwm","effort")
debrief_df <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 0, nrow = nrow(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests)))
this_task <- data.frame()

for (task in tasks) {
  #browser()
  this_task <- read.csv(paste0("../output/session1/",task,"/debrief.csv"))
  this_task <- this_task %>%
    select(-clarityRate) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(task, "_difficulty"), difficultyRate) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(task, "_fun"), funRate) #%>%
    # rename_with(~ paste0(task, "_clarity"), clarityRate)

  
  debrief_df <- cbind(debrief_df, this_task)
}

debrief_df_full <- cbind(data_day1_constrained_quadratic_prg_quests, debrief_df)

# Let's check the correlation
corr_data_subj_ratings_day1 <- correlation(debrief_df_full,method="spearman",p_adjust = "none")
```

# Attention checks (Day 1)

```{r}
## Load catch trials from all the tasks
foraging_catch <- read.csv("../output/session1/foraging_catch_trials.csv")
gng_catch <- read.csv("../output/session1/gng_catch_trials.csv")
rlwm_catch <- read.csv("../output/session1/rlwm_catch_trials.csv")
effort_catch <- read.csv("../output/session1/effort_catch_trials.csv")

# Questionnaires catch trials
quest_catch <- read.csv("../output/session1/quests_catch_trials.csv")

# helper: reshape each df to wide format
reshape_task <- function(df, taskname) {
  df %>%
    group_by(subjID) %>%
    mutate(trial_num = row_number()) %>%       # number catch trials per subject
    select(subjID, trial_num, correct) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = trial_num, 
                values_from = correct, 
                names_prefix = paste0(taskname, "_"))
}

effort_wide    <- reshape_task(effort_catch,    "effort")
rlwm_wide      <- reshape_task(rlwm_catch,      "rlwm")
gng_wide       <- reshape_task(gng_catch,       "gng")
foraging_wide  <- reshape_task(foraging_catch,  "foraging")

# merge all together by subjID
catch_tasks_df <- effort_wide %>%
  full_join(rlwm_wide, by = "subjID") %>%
  full_join(gng_wide, by = "subjID") %>%
  full_join(foraging_wide, by = "subjID")

catch_quests_tasks_df <- merge(
  catch_tasks_df,
  quest_catch,
  by = "subjID"
)


catch_quests_tasks_df <- catch_quests_tasks_df %>%
  mutate(across(-subjID, ~ as.logical(.))) %>%   # convert everything except subjID to TRUE/FALSE
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    failed_total = sum(c_across(-subjID) == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```
